subject: MSA + Order Form: proposal for physical injury / property damage exception

Subject: MSA / Order Form - question on physical injury/property damage carve-out

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement counsel reviewed the MSA + Order Form and flagged one key item: because our deployments interact with industrial control systems on customer sites, they need an explicit carve-out for physical injury and property damage from the MSA's liability cap and consequential damages exclusion.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept an exception that:
- excludes bodily injury and tangible property damage from the general liability cap and from any exclusion of consequential damages;
- provides a separate sub-cap tied to insurance (we proposed $5M) OR an uncapped obligation if caused by Redwood's gross negligence; and
- includes prompt notice and cooperation covenants in those scenarios.

Contracts copied here — please loop in legal if helpful. We need to close commercial terms by next week to hit our internal go-live.

Thanks,
Dana Myers
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Industrial

Dana — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Rachel (CS/implementation) to confirm operational impact.

Short answer: we understand why Acme is asking for the carve-out. Redwood's standard MSA limits liability to fees paid in the prior 12 months and disclaims consequential damages, but we have some flexibility for site-specific risk tied to physical harm. Marissa — can you propose language that balances Acme's safety needs and Redwood's enterprise insurance exposure?

Operational note for Rachel: if we accept any carve-out that creates a potential exposure > insurance, we should capture implementation constraints in the Order Form (on-site controls, access windows, indemnity triggers).

I'll aim to get a redline back to Dana and Contracts by tomorrow EOD.

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - proposed language for physical injury/property damage

Karthik / Dana — draft language below and attached a PDF with tracked redlines against Redwood_MSA_v3. Key points summarized first:

- Redwood is willing to carve out bodily injury and tangible property damage from the general limitation of liability, but only to the extent such loss is caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Redwood proposes an affirmative sub-cap of $5,000,000 for covered claims where liability arises from Redwood's negligence (subject to applicable insurance limits). For gross negligence or willful misconduct we will not rely on a monetary cap to the extent insurance would not cover the loss, but we prefer to keep a reasonable maximum tied to policy limits where practicable.
- We require prompt notice, control of defense (with Customer's right to participate), and normal cooperation obligations.
- For clarity, consequential damages language remains in place except that the carve-out expressly removes bodily injury and tangible property damage from the definition of excluded consequential damages.

Proposed contract language (redline-ready):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitations on liability set forth in Section 12 (Limitation of Liability) shall not apply to (a) claims for bodily injury or death of a person, or (b) direct physical damage to tangible property, to the extent such claims result from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. For claims arising from Redwood's ordinary negligence, Customer's aggregate recovery for such claims shall be capped at five million United States Dollars (US$5,000,000), which cap is intended to reflect Redwood's commercial insurance coverage.

Customer and Redwood shall provide prompt written notice of any claim subject to this paragraph, and Redwood shall have the right to control the defense of such claim with counsel of its choosing, provided that Customer may participate in the defense at its own expense.

For the avoidance of doubt, claims for bodily injury or tangible property damage shall not be treated as "consequential, incidental, indirect, exemplary, or punitive" damages under this Agreement."

Issues for Acme to consider: if Acme requires an unconditional uncapped liability for any physical damage irrespective of Redwood's culpability, that's not acceptable to Redwood. If Acme requires the carve-out to apply to subcontractors or third-party integrators, we need explicit specs and indemnities.

Please see attached Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf for inline edits and OrderForm_ACME_v2.docx with a note to add site controls.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-02T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form: proposal for physical injury / property damage exception

Dana — following up with a consolidated position after internal review. Appreciate the patience.

What Redwood can accept:
- The carve-out language proposed by Marissa above (excerpted) — i.e., bodily injury and tangible property damage are excluded from the general limitation of liability when caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- For ordinary negligence claims tied to physical harm, Redwood will accept a sub-cap of USD 5,000,000. That sub-cap is linked to Redwood's commercial insurance and reflects a compromise between Acme's risk tolerance and Redwood's underwriting.
- Contract language will include prompt notice, cooperation, and Redwood's right to control defense (Customer may participate at its own expense).
- We'll update the Order Form with operational mitigations (site access windows, implementation signoffs, and any specific safety controls) and require mutual acceptance of those specific controls prior to go-live.

What we cannot accept: an unconditional, uncapped liability for all physical/property claims irrespective of Redwood's fault, or language that expands contractor/subcontractor liability without technical specs and prior written agreement.

Next steps: if Acme agrees in principle, I will send the redlined MSA back for your comments and we can add the Order Form operational annex. If you'd prefer, we can do a 30-minute call tomorrow to get the final wording agreed.

Thanks — hoping we can close this week.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
